question: Should OpenClaw add a permanent manifest-gated plugin API and durable core safety-history surface now, or should this work be narrowed to an approved internal diagnostics contract first?
rationale: This PR adds a plugin manifest capability, public service-context API, persistent state schema, and user-facing operator surface; choosing the durable product and SDK boundary cannot be resolved mechanically from the patch.

options.title: Approve a narrow core contract
options.body: Define the supported plugin capability, payload privacy rules, ownership, and upgrade guarantees, then require the PR to implement that approved boundary.

options.title: Keep the first phase internal
options.body: Land only an owner-approved internal diagnostics seam and defer external plugin emission plus persistent operator history until their contracts are designed.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or defer the broad taxonomy until maintainers can sponsor a scoped observability roadmap item.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define the supported plugin capability, payload privacy rules, ownership, and upgrade guarantees, then require the PR to implement that approved boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: A named current-main owner could not be established from the supplied feature history, so this needs routing through the repository’s diagnostics/plugin-SDK ownership path.
